purpose: Exact provenance/reproduction of the zenith Koomen-derived grid consumed by Taylor's public halakhic_calc runtime; not a measurement-operator completion and not a fit.

taylorPublicRepository.runtimeInterpolation: RegularGridInterpolator over (sky altitude Z, azimuth offset T, solar altitude H) in log10(B), followed by 10**interpolated_value
taylorPublicRepository.runtimeSolarAltitude: sun = ephem.Sun(); sun.compute(obs); H = float(sun.alt); public calc_time.py contains no Observer.pressure override

primarySource.citation: M. J. Koomen et al., Measurements of the Brightness of the Twilight Sky, JOSA 42, 353-356 (1952), DOI 10.1364/JOSA.42.000353
primarySource.tableZenithColumn: P=90 degrees in Tables I and II

taylorTransformationReproduced.siteCombination: arithmetic mean of Sacramento Peak and Maryland B0

boundaries: This proves the zenith numerical lineage of Taylor's committed Koomen-derived grid; it does not establish the missing historical angular acceptance, exact spectral response, detector time response, calibration uncertainty, or historical geometric-vs-apparent H convention.

PyEphem's documented default Observer pressure is 1010 mbar and its body altitudes include atmospheric refraction unless pressure is set to zero. Because Taylor's audited public code does not set pressure, its runtime H is a refracted/apparent PyEphem altitude under the documented default. This statement is about Taylor's runtime convention, not the unknown 1952 historical H convention.
